questions.corrige_markdown: The Hajj is the annual pilgrimage to Mecca, made in the month of Dhul-Hijjah (the twelfth month of the Islamic year). It is the fifth pillar of Islam and is obligatory once in a lifetime for every adult Muslim who has the physical health and the financial means to make the journey and to provide for his family while away. The rites are performed in and around Mecca, at the Kaaba, Mina, Arafat and Muzdalifah, and follow the pattern taught by the Prophet Muhammad, which Muslims trace back to Ibrahim. It is different from the Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage, which can be made at any time of the year.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) How important is the Hajj in the practice of the Islamic Faith? [20 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The Hajj is a pillar of Islam and one of the greatest acts of worship. Its importance may be seen under the following headings.

**1. A religious duty.** It is commanded in the Quran (Surah Al Imran, 3, and Surah al-Hajj, 22). A Muslim who is able and neglects it fails in a basic duty, so the Hajj completes the practice of the faith, along with the shahadah, the prayer, zakat and fasting.

**2. Spiritual renewal and forgiveness.** According to hadith, a pilgrim whose Hajj is accepted returns free of sin like a newborn child. The pilgrim repents, prays, recites the Quran and gives up quarrels and bad speech. The standing at Arafat, the day of prayer and supplication, is the high point of the Hajj.

**3. Remembrance of Ibrahim and his family.** The rites recall the monotheistic faith of Ibrahim, Hajar and Ismail: the tawaf round the Kaaba, which Muslims believe was built by Ibrahim and Ismail, the running (sai) between Safa and Marwa, the well of Zamzam, the stoning of the pillars at Mina and the sacrifice, which recalls Ibrahim's obedience.

**4. Unity and equality.** Pilgrims of all races, nations and social classes wear the same simple white garments of ihram and perform the same rites together, which shows that all are equal before God. The Hajj makes the worldwide community (ummah) visible and strengthens the bonds among Muslims.

**5. Discipline and sacrifice.** The state of ihram forbids fighting, hunting, cutting hair and other things. The pilgrim must endure the crowds, the heat and the cost, which trains patience and self-control.

**6. Link with the Prophet.** The Prophet performed the Hajj and gave his Farewell Sermon at Arafat, which stressed the equality of all people and the sanctity of life and property. By following the rites, the pilgrim follows his example.

**7. Social and educational value.** The pilgrims exchange news and knowledge, and a returning pilgrim (hajji) is respected in the community. The Hajj is also a model of orderly worship on a large scale.

**Conclusion.** The Hajj is highly important in the practice of Islam: it is a pillar of the faith, a means of forgiveness and renewal, a reminder of Ibrahim and the Prophet and a visible sign of the unity of Muslims.
themes: A Level Religious Studies - five pillars of islam
